newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST - Manila 91-day T-bill rate seen falling.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Manila 91-day T-bill rate seen falling.

text.p: The 91-day Treasury bill rate could fall to 9.917 percent at the next auction from the previous 10.159 percent after the Central Bank lowered its interest rates, a Reuter poll of six financial institutions on Friday showed.
The Central Bank on Friday cut its overnight borrowing rate by 0.25 percentage point to 10.0 percent, the second since Tuesday when it cut rates by 0.1875 percentage-points.
The next T-bills auction is due to be held on Monday.
"It's (the central bank move) an indication that interest rates could still go down," a big bank dealer said.

Traders said banks continued to experience high liquidity which should nudge interest rates lower. Banks have been swamped with peso liquidity because they have been shying away from the term reverse repos which have a 20 percent tax.
The Central Bank is confident its rate cut will not cause harm on the peso because inflows are coming in, another dealer said.
Inflows are expected from the proceeds of Europeso issuances and overseas borrowings of banks and companies.
The Central Bank's move on Friday caught the market unprepared since it was expected to come next week, they said.
The big cut in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate was a result of the sharp fall in the 91-day T-bill rate to an average of 10.159 from 10.564 percent last Monday.
